items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: The interviewee narrates stories about Billy Cassand and his wife Louisa, stating 'His wife was named Louisa. She was a fine person.' and 'Louisa grabbed him and brought him on out.' There is no indication the interviewee personally knew or interacted with Louisa Armstrong; he is recounting third-pa

ctx.x: Billy Cassand had never been in Mississippi, you see. So they used his name on the car and he'd done that act on the stage, him and his wife. And he was forgetful, you know. His wife was named Louisa. She was a fine person. She was highly educated, you know. She learned him what he knew. He used to be a little shoeshine boy in Donisonville. And he had a big, funny looking mouth, you know. And he was really funny. He was apt and catching that foolishness. And she'd teach it to him. And towards last, they both was…
You remember any of his jokes or anything?
